sentences.zh: 乾化二年六月二日，庶人友珪弑逆，矯太祖詔，遣供奉官丁昭溥馳至東京，密令帝害博王友文。

translations.literal: On the second day of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, the commoner Yougui committed regicide; he forged an edict in the name of Taizu and dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital, secretly ordering the Emperor to kill Prince of Bo Youwen.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, the deposed Yougui murdered his sovereign; forging an edict as if from Taizu, he sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu racing to the Eastern Capital with secret orders for the Emperor to kill Prince of Bo Youwen.

sentences.zh: 友珪即位，以帝為東京留守，行開封府尹，檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Yougui took the throne and appointed the Emperor Eastern Capital custodian, acting Kaifeng prefect, and honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui acceded, he made the Emperor custodian of the Eastern Capital, acting prefect of Kaifeng, and honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 友珪以篡逆居位，群情不附。

translations.literal: Yougui held power by usurpation, and popular sentiment did not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui ruled by treason, and the realm would not rally to him.

sentences.zh: 會趙岩至東京，從帝私宴，因言及社稷事。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yan arrived at the Eastern Capital, he joined the Emperor at a private banquet and the talk turned to affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan came to the Eastern Capital; over a private banquet with the Emperor they spoke of the fate of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝以誠款謀之，岩曰：「此事易如反掌，成敗在招討楊令公之手，但得一言諭禁軍，其事立辦。

translations.literal: The Emperor laid out his sincerity in counsel; Yan said: "This matter is as easy as turning one's palm; success or failure lies in the hands of Pacification Commissioner Lord Yang—one word to the forbidden army and the affair is done at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor opened his heart in planning; Yan said: "This is easy as turning the hand; victory rests with Pacification Commissioner Yang—persuade the forbidden army and the thing is settled at once.

sentences.zh: 」岩時典禁軍，洎還洛，以謀告侍衛親軍袁象先。

translations.literal: " Yan then commanded the forbidden army; when he returned to Luoyang he disclosed the plot to Imperial Guard commander Yuan Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan held the forbidden army; back in Luoyang he told the plot to Imperial Guard commander Yuan Xiangxian.

sentences.zh: 帝令腹心馬慎交之魏州見師厚，且言成事之日，賜勞軍錢五十萬緡，仍許兼鎮。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent his trusted man Ma Shenjiao to Weizhou to see Shihou, saying that when the deed succeeded he would grant fifty thousand strings in army rewards and still permit him to hold two commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched his confidant Ma Shenjiao to Weizhou to win Shihou, promising fifty thousand strings in rewards on success and a second command besides.

sentences.zh: 慎交，燕人也，素有膽辨，乃說師厚曰：「郢王殺君害父，篡居大位，宮中荒淫，靡所不至。

translations.literal: Shenjiao, a man of Yan, had long been bold and eloquent; he urged Shihou: "Prince of Ying killed his lord and harmed his father, usurped the great throne, and in the palace indulges every debauch.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjiao, a Yan man known for nerve and speech, pressed Shihou: "Prince of Ying slew his sovereign and father, seized the throne, and now wallows in every palace excess.

sentences.zh: 洛下人情已去，東京物望所歸，公若因而成之，則有輔立之功，討賊之效。

translations.literal: Sentiment in Luoyang is already gone; the Eastern Capital holds the people's hopes—if you seize the moment, you will have the merit of aiding enthronement and the effect of punishing the traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang has turned away; all eyes are on the Eastern Capital—act now and you win the credit of raising a ruler and crushing a rebel.

sentences.zh: 」師厚猶豫未決，謂從事曰：「吾於郢王，君臣之分已定，無故改圖，人謂我何！

translations.literal: " Shihou still hesitated and said to his staff: "Between Prince of Ying and me the lord-subject bond is fixed; to change course without cause—what would men say of me!
translations.idiomatic: " Shihou wavered and told his staff: "Prince of Ying and I are already lord and subject; to shift without cause—what would people say!

sentences.zh: 」慎交曰：「郢王以子弑父，是曰元凶。

translations.literal: " Shenjiao said: "Prince of Ying as son slew his father—he is the arch rebel.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenjiao replied: "Prince of Ying murdered his father as a son—the chief villain.

sentences.zh: 均王為君為親，正名仗義。

translations.literal: Prince of Jun is ruler and kin; his name is righteous and his cause just.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jun stands for sovereign and family—right in name and in arms.

sentences.zh: 彼若一朝事成，令公何情自處！

translations.literal: If he succeeds in a morning, how will you, my lord, face yourself!
translations.idiomatic: If he wins overnight, what place will you have, my lord!

sentences.zh: 」師厚驚曰：「幾誤計耳！

translations.literal: " Shihou started and said: "I nearly took the wrong course!
translations.idiomatic: " Shihou cried: "I was on the verge of ruin!

sentences.zh: 」乃令小校王舜賢至洛，密與趙岩、袁象先圖議。

translations.literal: " He then sent junior officer Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to plot secretly with Zhao Yan and Yuan Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent junior officer Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to conspire quietly with Zhao Yan and Yuan Xiangxian.

sentences.zh: 時有左右龍驤都在東京，帝偽作友珪詔，遣還洛下。

translations.literal: At that time the Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies were at the Eastern Capital; the Emperor forged an edict in Yougui's name and sent them back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies were then at the Eastern Capital; the Emperor forged Yougui's edict and ordered them back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉重遇部下龍驤一指揮於懷州叛，經年搜捕其黨，帝因遣人激怒其眾曰：「郢王以龍驤軍嘗叛，追汝等洛下，將盡坑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, a Dragon-Prancing command under Liu Chongyu had rebelled at Huaizhou; for a year their partisans were hunted; the Emperor therefore sent men to inflame the troops, saying: "Prince of Ying, because the Dragon-Prancing Army once rebelled, is summoning you to Luoyang and will bury you all alive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Dragon-Prancing command under Liu Chongyu had mutinied at Huaizhou and been hunted a full year; the Emperor sent agents to stir them: "Prince of Ying means to drag you to Luoyang and slaughter every man, since Dragon-Prancing once rebelled.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，乃以偽昭示之。

translations.literal: " The next day the forged edict was shown them.
translations.idiomatic: " Next day he displayed the forged order.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》：《梁太祖實錄》：「丙戌，東京言龍驤軍準詔追赴西京，軍情不肯進發。

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian: Divergent Accounts》: 《Veritable Record of Emperor Taizu of Liang》: "On bingxu the Eastern Capital reported that the Dragon-Prancing Army, per edict, was to hurry to the Western Capital; the troops refused to march.
translations.idiomatic: (《Zizhi Tongjian: Divergent Accounts》: 《Veritable Record of Emperor Taizu of Liang》: "On bingxu the Eastern Capital reported Dragon-Prancing troops under orders for the Western Capital would not move.

sentences.zh: 」實友珪征之，非友貞偽作，但激怒言坑之耳。）〉

translations.literal: " Yougui actually summoned them; Youzhen did not forge it—only the incitement about burial alive.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Yougui truly summoned them; Youzhen did not forge the edict—only the threat of massacre was invented.)〉

sentences.zh: 諸軍憂恐，將校垂泣告帝，乞指生路。

translations.literal: The armies were anxious and afraid; officers wept and begged the Emperor to show them a way to live.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were terrified; commanders wept and pleaded for a path to survival.

sentences.zh: 帝諭之曰：「先帝三十餘年，經營社稷，千征萬戰，爾等皆會從行。

translations.literal: The Emperor addressed them: "The late Emperor for more than thirty years tended the altars of state, fought a thousand battles and ten thousand campaigns—you all marched with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told them: "For thirty years the late Emperor built the realm through endless campaigns—you marched at his side.

sentences.zh: 今日先帝尚落人奸計，爾等安所逃避。

translations.literal: Today even the late Emperor fell to traitors' schemes—where can you flee.
translations.idiomatic: Today even he was trapped by villains—there was nowhere to run.

sentences.zh: 」因出梁祖御容以示諸將，帝歔欷而泣曰：「郢王賊害君父，違天逆地，復欲屠滅親軍，爾等苟能自趨洛陽，擒取逆豎，告謝先帝，即轉禍為福矣！

translations.literal: " He then brought out Taizu's portrait to show the commanders; the Emperor sobbed and wept: "Prince of Ying as traitor harmed lord and father, defied Heaven and earth, and would again slaughter the imperial guard—if you can yourselves hurry to Luoyang, seize the rebel, and report to the late Emperor, you will turn calamity into blessing!
translations.idiomatic: " He displayed Taizu's portrait; weeping, he said: "Prince of Ying murdered sovereign and father, defied Heaven and earth, and now would butcher the guard—march on Luoyang, seize the rebel, and appease the late Emperor, and disaster becomes fortune!

sentences.zh: 」眾踴躍曰：「王言是也。

translations.literal: " The crowd leapt up and said: "Your Highness speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: " All cried: "Your Highness is right.

sentences.zh: 」皆呼萬歲，請帝為主，時友珪改元之二月十五日也。

translations.literal: " All shouted ten thousand years and asked the Emperor to be their lord—it was the fifteenth day of the second month of Yougui's reign era.
translations.idiomatic: " They shouted long life and begged him to lead them—the fifteenth day of Yougui's second regnal month.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣人告趙岩、袁象先、傅暉、朱圭等。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent word to Zhao Yan, Yuan Xiangxian, Fu Hui, Zhu Gui, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then notified Zhao Yan, Yuan Xiangxian, Fu Hui, Zhu Gui, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 十七日，象先引禁軍千人突入宮城，遂誅友珪。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth Yuan Xiangxian led a thousand forbidden troops into the palace city and killed Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth Yuan Xiangxian stormed the palace with a thousand guards and slew Yougui.

sentences.zh: 事定，象先遣趙岩齎傳國寶至東京，請帝即位於洛陽。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Xiangxian sent Zhao Yan bearing the imperial seal to the Eastern Capital, asking the Emperor to take the throne at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Xiangxian sent Zhao Yan with the imperial seal to the Eastern Capital, urging enthronement at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝報之曰：「夷門，太祖創業之地，居天下之衝，北拒並、汾，東至淮海，國家藩鎮，多在厥東，命將出師，利於便近，若都洛下，非良圖也。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied: "Yimen is where Taizu founded the enterprise; it sits at the hub of the realm, blocking Bing and Fen in the north and reaching the Huai-Hai in the east—most of the realm's commands lie east of it; dispatching generals is advantageous from nearby—if the capital were Luoyang, it would not be a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered: "Yimen is Taizu's foundation, the crossroads of the empire—blocking Shanxi in the north, reaching the coast in the east; most commands lie eastward, and campaigns are easier from there—Luoyang would be a poor capital.

sentences.zh: 公等如堅推戴，冊禮宜在東京，賊平之日，即謁洛陽陵廟。」

translations.literal: If you insist on pushing me, the investiture rites should be at the Eastern Capital; when the traitor is pacified, I will then visit Luoyang's imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: If you will force the crown on me, invest me at the Eastern Capital; when the rebel is gone, I shall pay homage at Luoyang's tombs."

sentences.zh: 是月，帝即位於東京，乃去珪曆之號，稱乾化三年。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor took the throne at the Eastern Capital, discarded Yougui's reign title, and called the year Qianhua 3.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was enthroned at the Eastern Capital, abolished Yougui's era, and proclaimed Qianhua 3.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: An edict read:

sentences.zh: 我國家賞功罰罪，必葉朝章，報德伸冤，敢欺天道。

translations.literal: Our state in rewarding merit and punishing crime must follow court statutes; in repaying grace and redressing wrong we dare not deceive Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: In reward and punishment our state must keep to law; in gratitude and vengeance we dare not mock Heaven.

sentences.zh: 苟顯違於法制，雖暫滯於歲時，終振大綱，須歸至理。

translations.literal: Though for a time one may seem to defy statute, though for a season delay, in the end the great outline is raised and reason restored.
translations.idiomatic: Even when law seems briefly set aside, the great order will be restored in time.

sentences.zh: 重念太祖皇帝，嘗開霸府，有事四方。

translations.literal: We recall that Emperor Taizu once opened the hegemon's bureau and had business in every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: We remember Taizu opening the hegemon's office and campaigning in every direction.

sentences.zh: 迨建皇朝，載遷都邑，每以主留重務，居守難才，慎擇親賢，方膺寄任。

translations.literal: When the imperial house was founded the capital moved; each time the weight of staying behind was hard, and kin of merit were chosen for the charge.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was founded the seat moved; the custodian's burden was always heavy, and trusted princes were chosen to bear it.

sentences.zh: 故博王友文，才兼文武，識達古今，俾分憂於在浚之郊，亦共理於興王之地，一心無易，二紀於茲。

translations.literal: Thus Prince of Bo Youwen, gifted in civil and military arts and versed in past and present, was sent to share cares on the outskirts of Jun and to co-rule the land where the dynasty rose—his heart unchanged for two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bo Youwen, skilled in letters and arms and wise in history, shared rule at Jun and in the founding lands—loyal through two reigns.

sentences.zh: 嘗施惠於士民，實有勞於家國。

translations.literal: He once showed grace to officers and people and truly labored for house and state.
translations.idiomatic: He had shown kindness to soldiers and civilians and truly served the realm.

sentences.zh: 去歲郢王友珪，常懷逆節，已露凶鋒，將不利於君親，欲竊窺於神器。

translations.literal: Last year Prince of Ying Yougui long harbored treason, already bared his murderous edge, intending harm to lord and kin and coveting the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Prince of Ying Yougui nursed rebellion, bared his blade, and aimed at kin and throne alike.

sentences.zh: 此際值先皇寢疾，大漸日臻，博王乃密上封章，請嚴宮禁，因以萊州刺史授於郢王友珪，才睹宣頭，俄行大逆。

translations.literal: Just then the late Emperor lay gravely ill; Prince of Bo secretly memorialized to tighten the palace guard, and the office of Laizhou prefect was granted Prince of Ying Yougui—the proclamation had scarcely been read when the great crime was done.
translations.idiomatic: As the late Emperor lay dying, Prince of Bo secretly asked to seal the palace and gave Yougui the Laizhou post—hardly was the order read when the atrocity struck.

sentences.zh: 豈有自縱兵於內殿，卻翻事於東都，又矯詔書，枉加刑戮，仍奪博王封爵，又改姓名，冤恥兩深，欺誑何極。

translations.literal: How could he loose troops in the inner hall yet turn the affair to the Eastern Capital, forge edicts, impose wrongful execution, strip Prince of Bo's rank, and change his name—double deep in wrong and deceit beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He unleashed troops in the inner hall, shifted blame eastward, forged orders, executed the innocent, stripped Prince of Bo's titles, and changed his name—outrage piled on fraud without limit.

sentences.zh: 伏賴上穹垂祐，宗社降靈。

translations.literal: We relied on Heaven above to show favor and the altars to send blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favored us and the spirits aided the realm.

sentences.zh: 俾中外以葉謀，致遐邇之共怒，尋平內難，獲剿元凶，既雪恥於同天，且免譏於共國。

translations.literal: Within and without they plotted together; far and near shared rage; soon the inner trouble was pacified and the arch rebel cut down—shame washed away under one sky and reproach among the states avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country conspired; the empire raged; the revolt was crushed and the chief villain slain—honor restored under Heaven, scandal among the states averted.

sentences.zh: 朕方期遁世，敢竊臨人，遽迫推崇，爰膺纘嗣。

translations.literal: We had hoped to withdraw from the world and dared not usurp rule over men; suddenly pressed and pushed, we accepted succession.
translations.idiomatic: We meant to leave public life and dared not rule men; forced by acclaim, we took the succession.

sentences.zh: 冤憤既伸於幽顯，霈澤宜及於下泉。

translations.literal: With grievance answered in shade and light, grace should reach even the lower springs.
translations.idiomatic: Now that justice reaches the living and the dead, mercy should reach below as well.

sentences.zh: 博王宜復官爵，仍令有司擇日歸葬雲。

translations.literal: Prince of Bo should have his offices and titles restored and the authorities should choose a day for burial at Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bo's rank should be restored and the rites office should set a day for burial at Yun.

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，製曰：「朕仰膺天眷，近雪家仇，旋聞將相之謀，請紹祖宗之業。

translations.literal: On dingwei in the third month an ordinance stated: "We bear Heaven's favor, have lately avenged our house, and soon heard that generals and ministers urged us to continue the ancestors' enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the third month an ordinance said: "Heaven has favored us; we have avenged our kin and now ministers urge us to inherit the ancestral work.

sentences.zh: 群情見迫，三讓莫從，隻受推崇，懼不負荷。

translations.literal: Popular pressure left no room for three refusals; we alone received the push and fear we cannot bear the load.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude would not let us refuse thrice; we take the burden alone and fear we may fail it.

sentences.zh: 方欲烝嘗寢廟，禋類郊丘，合征文體之辭，用表事神之敬。

translations.literal: We mean to offer at the ancestral shrine and perform suburban rites, gathering literary forms to show reverence to the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: We shall sacrifice at the temple and worship at the suburbs, gathering proper texts to honor the gods.

sentences.zh: 其或於文尚淺，在理未周，亦冀隨時，別圖製義。

translations.literal: If the wording is still shallow or the reasoning incomplete, we hope in time to revise the ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Where the prose is thin or the logic unfinished, we may revise the text as occasion allows.

sentences.zh: 雖臣子行孝，重更名於已孤；

translations.literal: Though a subject's filial piety may rename him after his parents are gone,
translations.idiomatic: A son may change his name in mourning,

sentences.zh: 而君父稱尊，貴難知而易避。

translations.literal: yet to honor lord and father is hard to know and easy to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: yet titles for sovereign and father are perilous to speak and best left untouched.

sentences.zh: 今則虔遵古典，詳考前聞，允諧龜筮之占，庶合帝王之道。

translations.literal: Now we reverently follow the classics and examine former records, hoping the tortoise and milfoil agree and the way of emperors is met.
translations.idiomatic: We now follow the classics and ancient precedent, trusting the omens and the imperial way align.

sentences.zh: 載惟涼德，尤愧嘉名，中外群僚，當體朕意。

translations.literal: Our modest virtue is especially shamed by a fine name; officials within and without should grasp our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Our meager virtue ill suits a glorious name; let all officials understand our mind.

sentences.zh: 宜改名鍠。

translations.literal: The name should be changed to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Let the name be changed to Huang.

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，以天雄軍節度使、充潞州行營都招討使、開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、兼侍中、弘農郡王楊師厚為檢校太師，兼中書令，進封鄴王。

translations.literal: " On gengxu Tianxiong Military Commissioner, Pacification Commissioner for the Luzhou campaign headquarters, Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, Honorary Grand Tutor, Minister of Works, Prince of Hongnong Yang Shihou was made Honorary Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and advanced to Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengxu Yang Shihou, commissioner of Tianxiong, commander of the Luzhou campaign, and Prince of Hongnong, became Honorary Grand Preceptor and Grand Counselor and was advanced to Prince of Ye.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以夏州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事李仁福為檢校太師，進封隴西郡王。

translations.literal: On renxu Xiazhou Military Commissioner, Honorary Grand Tutor, Co-Grand Counselor Li Renfu was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and advanced to Prince of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Li Renfu of Xiazhou, Honorary Grand Tutor and co-counselor, became Honorary Grand Preceptor and Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以邢州保義軍留後、檢校太保戴思遠為檢校太傅，充邢州節度使。

translations.literal: On wuchen Xingzhou Baoyi Army acting commissioner, Honorary Palace Attendant Dai Siyuan was made Honorary Grand Mentor and full Xingzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Dai Siyuan, acting Baoyi commissioner at Xingzhou, became Honorary Grand Mentor and commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以鎮東軍節度副使、充兩浙西面都指揮使、行睦州刺史馬綽為檢校太傅、同平章事，領秦州雄武軍節度使，進封開國候。

translations.literal: On gengwu Zhendong Military Commissioner deputy, commander of the Two Zhes western front, acting Muzhou prefect Ma Chuo was made Honorary Grand Mentor and Co-Grand Counselor, given Qinzhou Xiongwu Military Commissioner, and advanced to Marquis of the Opening State.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Ma Chuo, Zhendong deputy and Two Zhes commander, became Honorary Grand Mentor and co-counselor, took Xiongwu at Qinzhou, and was made Marquis of the Opening State.

sentences.zh: 是月，文武百官上言，請以九月十二日帝降誕日為明聖節，休假三日。

translations.literal: That month civil and military officials memorialized that the twelfth day of the ninth month, the Emperor's birthday, be made Bright Sage Festival with three days' leave.
translations.idiomatic: That month officials asked that the Emperor's birthday, the twelfth of the ninth month, be Bright Sage Festival with three days off.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸未，以西京內外諸軍馬步軍都指揮使、檢校司徒、左龍虎統軍、濮陽郡開國侯袁象先為特進、檢校太保、同平章事，充鎮南軍節度、江南西道觀察處置等使、開封尹、判在京馬步諸軍事，進封開國公，增食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on guiwei, Western Capital inner and outer horse and foot commander, Honorary Minister of Works, Left Dragon-Tiger commander, Marquis of Puyang Yuan Xiangxian was made Special Advancement, Honorary Palace Attendant, Co-Grand Counselor, Zhennan Military Commissioner and Jiangnan West Circuit observation commissioner, Kaifeng prefect, and judge of capital horse and foot affairs, advanced to Duke of the Opening State with an added thousand-household fief.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the fourth month Yuan Xiangxian, commander of Western Capital forces, became Special Advancement, Honorary Palace Attendant, co-counselor, Zhennan commissioner, Jiangnan West observer, Kaifeng prefect, and judge of capital armies, and was made Duke of the Opening State with a thousand added households.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，宣義軍節度副大使、知節度事、鄭滑濮等州觀察使、檢校太傅、長沙郡開國公羅周翰加特進、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: On dingyou Xuanyi Military Commissioner deputy, knowing commissioner affairs, Zheng-Hua-Pu observer, Honorary Grand Mentor, Duke of Changsha Luo Zhouhan was given Special Advancement and made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Luo Zhouhan, Xuanyi deputy and Zheng-Hua-Pu observer, received Special Advancement and the post of Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant.

sentences.zh: 五月乙巳，天雄軍節度使楊師厚及劉守奇率魏、博、邢、洺、徐、兗、鄆、滑之眾十萬討鎮州。

translations.literal: On yisi in the fifth month Tianxiong Military Commissioner Yang Shihou and Liu Shouqi led a hundred thousand from Wei, Bo, Xing, Ming, Xu, Yan, Yun, and Hua to attack Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the fifth month Yang Shihou and Liu Shouqi marched a hundred thousand from eight prefectures against Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，營於鎮之南門外。

translations.literal: On gengxu they encamped outside Zhen's south gate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu they camped south of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，晉將史建瑭自趙州領騎五百入於鎮州，師厚知其有備，自九門移軍於下博。

translations.literal: On renzi Jin general Shi Jianya led five hundred cavalry from Zhaozhou into Zhenzhou; Shihou knew they were prepared and moved his army from Jiumen to Xiabo.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Shi Jianya of Jin entered Zhenzhou with five hundred horse; Shihou, seeing them ready, shifted from Jiumen to Xiabo.

sentences.zh: 劉守奇以一軍自貝州掠冀州衡水、阜城，陷下博。

translations.literal: Liu Shouqi with one army from Beizhou raided Hengshui and Fucheng in Jizhou and took Xiabo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouqi swept from Beizhou through Jizhou's Hengshui and Fucheng and seized Xiabo.

sentences.zh: 師厚自弓高渡御河，逼滄州，張萬進懼，送款，師厚表請以萬進為青州節度使，以劉守奇為滄州節度使。

translations.literal: Shihou crossed the Imperial River at Gonggao and pressed Cangzhou; Zhang Wanjin was afraid and submitted; Shihou memorialized to make Wanjin Qingzhou Military Commissioner and Shouqi Cangzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou crossed the Imperial River at Gonggao and threatened Cangzhou until Zhang Wanjin surrendered; he asked Wanjin for Qingzhou and Shouqi for Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太祖皇帝六月二日大忌。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The great anniversary of Emperor Taizu falls on the second day of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The second day of the sixth month is Taizu's death anniversary.

sentences.zh: 朕聞姬周已還，並用通喪之禮，炎漢之後，方行易月之儀。

translations.literal: We hear that after the Zhou of Ji returned, universal mourning was used; after the Han of Yan, the month-shortening rite was practiced.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou returned home they observed full mourning; after Han they shortened the mourning month.

sentences.zh: 歷代相沿，萬幾斯重，遂為故實，難遽改更。

translations.literal: Dynasties have followed one another; the myriad tasks weigh heavily—thus it became precedent, hard to change hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty kept the custom; state business is weighty—the precedent stands and cannot be lightly broken.

sentences.zh: 朕頃遘家冤，近平內難，倏臨祥製，俯迫忌辰，音容永遠而莫追，號感彌深而難抑。

translations.literal: We have lately met with family wrong and nearly faced inner strife; suddenly the auspicious mourning garb presses upon the anniversary; his face is forever gone and cannot be pursued, our cries ever deeper and hard to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from family bloodshed and inner turmoil, we face mourning garb and the anniversary together; his countenance is gone beyond recall and grief will not be stilled.

sentences.zh: 將欲表宅憂於中禁，是宜輟聽政於外朝，雖異常儀，願申罔極。

translations.literal: We wish to show dwelling in grief within the inner palace; it is fitting to suspend audience in the outer court—though the rite is irregular, we beg to express boundless sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: We would mourn within the palace and suspend court without—irregular, yet it expresses utmost filial grief.

sentences.zh: 宜輟五月二十二日至六月二十九日朝參，軍機急切公事，即不得留滯，並仰畫時聞奏施行。

translations.literal: Court attendance should be suspended from the twenty-second day of the fifth month to the twenty-ninth of the sixth; urgent military business must not be delayed and should be reported and executed at once."
translations.idiomatic: Suspend audiences from the twenty-second of the fifth month through the twenty-ninth of the sixth; urgent military matters must not wait and are to be reported and acted on immediately."

sentences.zh: 」宰臣文武百官三上表，以國忌廢務多日，請依舊制。

translations.literal: Chancellors and civil and military officials thrice memorialized that state business had been suspended many days for the national anniversary and asked to follow the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors and officials thrice begged to resume the old schedule, saying the mourning closure had lasted too long.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「朕聞禮非天降，固可酌於人情，事係孝思，諒無妨於國體。

translations.literal: The edict in reply stated: "We hear that ritual is not dropped from Heaven and may be weighed against human feeling; affairs of filial thought surely need not harm the body politic.
translations.idiomatic: The reply read: "Rites are not heaven-sent and may bend to human feeling; filial duty need not harm the state.

sentences.zh: 今以甫臨忌日，暫輟視朝，冀全哀感之情，用表始終之節。

translations.literal: Now as the anniversary nears we briefly suspend court, hoping to preserve the feeling of grief and show constancy from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: As the anniversary approaches we pause court briefly to honor grief and show constancy.

sentences.zh: 宰臣等累陳章表，備述古今，慮以萬幾之繁，議以五月之請。

translations.literal: The chancellors repeatedly submitted memorials, setting forth past and present, fearing the press of the myriad tasks and urging the request of the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers repeatedly cited precedent, fearing the press of affairs and urging the May schedule.

sentences.zh: 雖茲懇切，難盡允俞，況保身方荷於洪基，敢言過毀，而權制獲申於至性，必在得中。

translations.literal: Though their plea was earnest, it could not all be granted; moreover we now bear the great foundation—how dare we speak of excess mourning—yet the temporary rule may express utmost feeling and must hit the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Their plea was earnest but could not be fully granted; we bear the foundation now and dare not indulge excess—yet temporary mourning must find the mean.

sentences.zh: 宜自今月二十九日輟至六月七日，無煩抑請，深體朕懷。」

translations.literal: From the twenty-ninth of this month until the seventh of the sixth month—no further pleas; deeply grasp our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Suspend court only from this month's twenty-ninth to the seventh of the sixth—no more petitions; understand our heart."

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，以滄州順化軍節度使、並潞鎮定副招討使、檢校太傅、同平章事張萬進為青州節度使。

translations.literal: On wuzi in the sixth month Cangzhou Shunhua Military Commissioner, deputy Pacification Commissioner for Bing-Lu-Zhen-Ding, Honorary Grand Mentor, Co-Grand Counselor Zhang Wanjin was made Qingzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Zhang Wanjin of Cangzhou became commissioner of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋九月甲辰，以光祿大夫、守御史大夫、吳興郡開國侯姚洎為中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiachen, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, acting Censor-in-Chief, Marquis of Wuxing Yao Ji was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the ninth month Yao Ji, Grandee of Splendid Happiness and acting censor-in-chief, became vice director of the Secretariat and grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚午，以前鄆州節度、檢校司徒、食邑二千戶、福王友璋為許州節度使，檢校太保。

translations.literal: On gengwu in the twelfth month former Yunzhou Military Commissioner, Honorary Minister of Works, fief of two thousand households, Prince of Fu Youzhang was made Xuzhou Military Commissioner and Honorary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the twelfth month Prince of Fu Youzhang, former Yunzhou commissioner, became Xuzhou commissioner and Honorary Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 是月，晉王收幽州，執偽燕主劉守光及其父仁恭歸晉陽。

translations.literal: That month the Prince of Jin took Youzhou and brought the false Yan ruler Liu Shouguang and his father Rengong to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Prince of Jin captured Youzhou and brought the puppet Yan ruler Liu Shouguang and his father Rengong to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 乾化四年春正月壬寅，以青州節度使張萬進為兗州節度使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of Qianhua 4, on renyin, Qingzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Wanjin was made Yanzhou Military Commissioner and Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianhua 4, on renyin, Zhang Wanjin of Qingzhou became Yanzhou commissioner and Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 二月甲戌，以感化軍節度使、華商等州觀察使、檢校太傅、同平章事、太原郡開國公康懷英為大安尹，充永平軍節度使，大安金棣等州觀察處置使。

translations.literal: On jiaxu in the second month Ganhua Military Commissioner, observer of Hua and Shang, Honorary Grand Mentor, Co-Grand Counselor, Duke of Taiyuan Kang Huaiying was made prefect of Da'an, Yongping Military Commissioner, and observer of Da'an, Jin, and Di.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Kang Huaiying, Ganhua commissioner and Duke of Taiyuan, became prefect of Da'an and Yongping commissioner over Da'an, Jin, and Di.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁丑，以守司空、平章事於兢為工部侍郎，尋眨萊州司馬，以其挾私與軍校遷改故也。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the fourth month of summer Acting Minister of Works and Grand Counselor Yu Jing was made Vice Minister of Works; soon he was demoted to Luzhou marshal for favoring private ties in promoting military officers.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Yu Jing, acting minister of works and grand counselor, became vice minister of works, then was exiled to Luzhou as marshal for nepotism toward officers.

sentences.zh: 是日，以行營左先鋒馬軍使、濮州刺史王彥章為澶州刺史，充行營先鋒步軍都指揮使，加光祿大夫、檢校太保，封開國伯；

translations.literal: That day campaign Left Vanguard Horse Commander and Puzhou prefect Wang Yanzhang was made Cizhou prefect and campaign vanguard foot commander, given Grandee of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Earl of the Opening State;
translations.idiomatic: That day Wang Yanzhang, left vanguard horse commander and Puzhou prefect, became Cizhou prefect and foot vanguard of the campaign, Grandee of Splendid Happiness, Honorary Palace Attendant, and Earl of the Opening State;

sentences.zh: 以永平軍節度使、檢校太傅、同平章事劉鄩為開封尹，遙領鎮南軍節度使。

translations.literal: Yongping Military Commissioner, Honorary Grand Mentor, Co-Grand Counselor Liu Yan was made Kaifeng prefect and titular Zhennan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan of Yongping became Kaifeng prefect with titular command of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 五月癸丑，朔方軍留後、檢校司徒韓洙起復，授朔方軍節度使，檢校太保。

translations.literal: On guichou in the fifth month Shuofang acting commissioner, Honorary Minister of Works Han Zhu was recalled to service and made Shuofang Military Commissioner and Honorary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Han Zhu of Shuofang left mourning and became Shuofang commissioner and Honorary Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，晉王率師自黃澤嶺東下，寇邢、洺，魏博節度使楊師厚軍於漳水之東。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Prince of Jin led troops east from Huangzeling, raided Xing and Ming; Weibo Military Commissioner Yang Shihou encamped east of the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Prince of Jin marched east from Huangzeling against Xing and Ming; Yang Shihou of Weibo camped east of the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 晉將曹進金來奔，晉軍遂退。

translations.literal: Jin general Cao Jinjin came over; the Jin army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jinjin of Jin defected; the Jin forces retreated.

sentences.zh: 九月，徐州節度使王殷反。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Xuzhou Military Commissioner Wang Yin rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Yin, commissioner of Xuzhou, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以福王友璋鎮徐方，殷不受代，乃下詔削奪殷在身官爵，仍令卻還本姓蔣，便委友璋及天平軍節度使牛存節、開封尹劉鄩等進軍攻討。

translations.literal: The court had sent Prince of Fu Youzhang to hold Xuzhou; Yin would not yield; an edict stripped Yin of all offices and ranks, restored his original surname Jiang, and ordered Youzhang, Niucunjie of Tianping, Liu Yan of Kaifeng, and others to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court had posted Prince of Fu Youzhang at Xuzhou; Yin refused replacement; an edict stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Youzhang, Niucunjie, Liu Yan, and others against him.

sentences.zh: 是時，蔣殷求救於淮南，楊溥遣大將朱瑾率眾來援，存節等逆擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Jiang Yin sought aid from Huainan; Yang Pu sent Grand General Zhu Jin with troops; Niucunjie and others met and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yin called on Huainan; Yang Pu sent Zhu Jin; Niucunjie and the rest routed the relief force.

sentences.zh: 貞明元年春，牛存節、劉鄩拔徐州，逆賊將殷舉族自燔而死，於火中得其屍，梟首以獻。

translations.literal: In spring of Zhenming 1, Niucunjie and Liu Yan took Xuzhou; the rebel general Yin and his clan burned themselves to death; his corpse was taken from the fire and his head presented.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Zhenming 1, Niucunjie and Liu Yan seized Xuzhou; Yin and his kin immolated themselves; his body was pulled from the flames and his head sent in.

sentences.zh: 詔福王友璋赴鎮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Fu Youzhang to proceed to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Prince of Fu Youzhang to his post.

sentences.zh: 閏二月甲午，延州節度使、太原西面招討應接使、檢校太師、兼中書令、渤海郡王高萬興進封渤海王。

translations.literal: On jiawu in the intercalary second month Yanzhou Military Commissioner, western Pacification and liaison commissioner for Taiyuan, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, Prince of Bohai Gao Wanxing was advanced to Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the intercalary second month Gao Wanxing of Yanzhou, western liaison commissioner for Taiyuan, became Prince of Bohai outright.

sentences.zh: 三月辛酉朔，以天平軍節度副大使、知節度事、兼淮南西北面行營招討應接等使、檢校太傅、同平章事牛存節為檢校太尉，加食邑一千戶，賞平徐之功也。

translations.literal: On xinyou, first day of the third month, Tianping Military Commissioner deputy, knowing commissioner affairs, Northwestern Huainan campaign Pacification and liaison commissioner, Honorary Grand Mentor, Co-Grand Counselor Niucunjie was made Honorary Grand Tutor with an added thousand-household fief, rewarding the pacification of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, first of the third month, Niucunjie of Tianping became Honorary Grand Tutor with a thousand added households for crushing Xu.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以右僕射兼門下侍郎、同平章事、監修國史、判度支趙光逢為太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: On dingmao Right Vice President of the Secretariat, Concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, Co-Grand Counselor, Compiler of National History, and Controller of Revenue Zhao Guangfeng was made Heir Apparent Grand Mentor and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zhao Guangfeng, right vice president and co-counselor, retired as Heir Apparent Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使楊師厚薨，輟視朝三日。

translations.literal: Weibo Military Commissioner Yang Shihou died; court audiences were suspended three days.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou of Weibo died; the court mourned three days without audience.

sentences.zh: 初，師厚握強兵，據重鎮，每邀朝廷姑息，及薨，輟視朝三日，或者以為天意。

translations.literal: Earlier Shihou held a strong army and a weighty command, often demanding indulgence from court; when he died and audiences were suspended three days, some took it as Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou had long held Weibo's armies and bullied the court for concessions; when he died and mourning closed court three days, some called it Heaven's judgment.

sentences.zh: 租庸使趙岩、租庸判官邵讚獻議於帝曰：「魏博六州，精兵數萬，蠹害唐室百有餘年。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Zhao Yan and transport judge Shao Zan offered counsel to the Emperor: "The six prefectures of Weibo hold tens of thousands of elite troops that have harmed the Tang house for more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan and Shao Zan urged the Emperor: "Weibo's six prefectures field tens of thousands of veterans who have plagued the Tang for a century.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威前恭後倨，太祖每深含怒。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei was deferential then arrogant; Taizu each time swallowed deep anger.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei bowed first and defied later; Taizu nursed wrath each time.

sentences.zh: 太祖屍未屬纊，師厚即肆陰謀。

translations.literal: Taizu's corpse was not yet wrapped in silks when Shihou at once plotted in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Before Taizu's body was shrouded, Shihou was already scheming.

sentences.zh: 蓋以地廣兵強，得肆其志，不如分削，使如身使臂，即無不從也。

translations.literal: Because the land was broad and troops strong he could indulge his will—better to divide and pare so that like arm and hand they would not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: His vast territory and huge host let him do as he pleased—split the command so the court commands it like an arm, never a rival.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以此時製之，寧知後之人不為楊師厚耶！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not restrain them now, who knows whether later men will not become another Yang Shihou!
translations.idiomatic: Restrain them now, or the next man may be another Yang Shihou!

sentences.zh: 若分割相、魏為兩鎮，則朝廷無北顧之患矣！

translations.literal: If Xiang and Wei are split into two commands, the court need no longer fear the north.
translations.idiomatic: Divide Xiang and Wei into two commands and the north ceases to threaten the throne.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Well said.

sentences.zh: 」即以平盧軍節度使賀德倫為天雄軍節度使，遣劉鄩率兵六萬屯河朔。

translations.literal: " Pinglu Military Commissioner He Delun was made Tianxiong Military Commissioner and Liu Yan was sent with sixty thousand troops to garrison Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: " He Delun of Pinglu became Tianxiong commissioner; Liu Yan marched sixty thousand to camp in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「分疆裂土，雖賞勳勞；

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Dividing territory rewards merit;
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Partitioning land rewards service;

sentences.zh: 建節屯師，亦從機便。

translations.literal: establishing commands and stationing troops also follows expedience.
translations.idiomatic: raising commands and posting armies follows the moment.

sentences.zh: 比者魏博一鎮，巡屬六州，為河朔之大藩，實國家之巨鎮。

translations.literal: Lately the single Weibo command oversaw six prefectures—a great bulwark of Hebei and a giant town of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo had been one command over six prefectures—the greatest fortress of the north.

sentences.zh: 所分憂寄，允謂重難；

translations.literal: The charge entrusted was truly weighty;
translations.idiomatic: Its burden was immense;

sentences.zh: 將葉事機，須期通濟。

translations.literal: to abandon opportunity requires timely remedy.
translations.idiomatic: to miss the moment demands a swift cure.

sentences.zh: 但緣鎮、定賊境，最為魏、博親鄰；

translations.literal: But because Zhen and Ding border the enemy, they are Weibo and Bo's nearest kin;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Ding border the enemy and are Weibo's closest neighbors;

sentences.zh: 其次相、衛兩州，皆控澤潞山口。

translations.literal: next Xiang and Wei two prefectures both control the Zelu mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang and Wei guard the Zelu passes.

sentences.zh: 兩道並連於晉土，分頭常寇於魏封。

translations.literal: Both circuits adjoin Jin territory and often raid Weibo's borders.
translations.idiomatic: Both touch Jin lands and raid Weibo without cease.

sentences.zh: 既須日有戰爭，未若懼分節制。

translations.literal: War is daily; better to fear divided command.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting is daily; split command lest they exhaust themselves.

sentences.zh: 免勞兵力，因奔命於兩途；

translations.literal: Spare the troops' labor, lest they run themselves ragged on two roads;
translations.idiomatic: Save the soldiers from running themselves to death on two fronts;

sentences.zh: 稍泰人心，俾安居於終日。

translations.literal: ease hearts somewhat so they may live in peace at last.
translations.idiomatic: steady morale so the region can breathe.

sentences.zh: 其相州宜建節度為昭德軍。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou should have a command established as Zhaode Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou shall become the Zhaode Army command.

sentences.zh: 以澶、衛兩州為屬郡，以張筠為相州節度使。」

translations.literal: Cang and Wei are to be subject prefectures; Zhang Jun is made Xiangzhou Military Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Cang and Wei are subordinate; Zhang Jun is commissioner of Xiang."

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏博軍亂，囚節度使賀德倫。

translations.literal: On jichou the Weibo army mutinied and imprisoned Military Commissioner He Delun.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Weibo troops rebelled and seized He Delun.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷既分魏博六州為兩鎮，命劉鄩統大軍屯於南樂，以討王熔為名，遣澶州刺史、行營先鋒步軍都指揮使王彥章領龍驤五百騎先入於魏州，屯於金波亭。

translations.literal: The court had divided Weibo's six prefectures into two commands, ordered Liu Yan to lead the great army at Nanle in the name of attacking Wang Rong, and sent Cizhou Military Commissioner and campaign vanguard foot commander Wang Yanzhang with five hundred Dragon-Prancing cavalry into Weizhou first, encamped at Jinbo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The court had split Weibo, sent Liu Yan to Nanle ostensibly against Wang Rong, and Wang Yanzhang with five hundred Dragon-Prancing horse into Weizhou to camp at Jinbo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 詔以魏州軍兵之半隸於相州，並徙其家焉。

translations.literal: An edict placed half of Weizhou's troops under Xiangzhou and moved their families as well.
translations.idiomatic: Half of Weizhou's soldiers were assigned to Xiangzhou and their families moved with them.

sentences.zh: 又遣主者檢察魏之帑廩。

translations.literal: Inspectors were also sent to examine Weibo's treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Auditors were sent to inventory Weibo's stores.

sentences.zh: 既而德倫促諸軍上路，姻族辭決，哭聲盈巷。

translations.literal: Then Delun urged the armies to march; kin took leave with weeping that filled the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Delun ordered the troops on the road; families wailed in every street.

sentences.zh: 其徒乃相聚而謀曰：「朝廷以我軍府強盛，故設法殘破，況我六州，歷代藩府，軍門父子，姻族相連，未嘗遠出河門，離親去族，一旦遷於外郡，生不如死。

translations.literal: The men then gathered and plotted: "The court, because our command is strong, contrived to ruin us; moreover our six prefectures for generations were a frontier command—fathers and sons in the army, kin by marriage—never far from Hemen, never leaving kin; suddenly to move to outer commands—better dead than alive.
translations.idiomatic: They muttered: "The court means to break us because we are strong; six generations we held the gate, kin in every company—never sent beyond Hemen—and now they tear us away; death is kinder.

sentences.zh: 」三月二十九日夜，魏軍乃作亂，放火大掠，首攻龍驤軍，王彥章斬關而遁。

translations.literal: " On the night of the twenty-ninth of the third month the Weibo troops mutinied, set fires, and plundered greatly; they first attacked the Dragon-Prancing Army; Wang Yanzhang cut through the gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth of the third month Weibo rose, burned, and looted; they struck Dragon-Prancing first; Wang Yanzhang hacked his way out and escaped.

sentences.zh: 遲明，殺德倫親軍五百餘人於牙城，執德倫置之樓上。

translations.literal: At dawn they killed more than five hundred of Delun's personal guard at the headquarters and seized Delun on the tower.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they slaughtered five hundred of Delun's guard at headquarters and held him on the tower.

sentences.zh: 有效節軍校張彥者，最為粗暴，膽氣伏人，乃率無賴輩數百，止其剽掠。

translations.literal: A valiant command officer Zhang Yan, most violent, whose courage subdued men, then led several hundred ruffians and stopped the pillage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, a brutal officer who cowed the host, rallied hundreds of ruffians and halted the sack.

sentences.zh: 是日，魏之士庶被屠戮者，不可勝計。

translations.literal: That day the gentlemen and commoners of Wei who were butchered could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: That day the dead of Weizhou could not be numbered.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，遣使齎詔安撫，

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he sent an envoy with an edict to pacify them,
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the Emperor sent an envoy with soothing orders,

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈See also:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：夏四月，帝遣供奉官扈異撫諭魏軍。）〉

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: In the fourth month of summer the Emperor sent Palace Attendant Hu Yi to comfort the Weibo troops.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: That fourth month the Emperor sent Hu Yi to reassure Weibo's army.)〉

sentences.zh: 仍許張彥除郡厚賜，將士優賞。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan was still to be made prefect with rich gifts, and the officers and soldiers generously rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan was still offered a prefecture and rich gifts, the troops generous bounty.

sentences.zh: 彥等不遜，投詔於地，侮罵詔使，因迫德倫飛奏，請卻復相、衛，抽退劉鄩軍。

translations.literal: Yan and the rest were insubordinate, threw the edict to the ground, insulted the envoy, and forced Delun to memorialize urgently asking that Xiang and Wei be restored and Liu Yan's army withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yan defied the court, trampled the edict, cursed the envoy, and made Delun demand Xiang and Wei back and Liu Yan's withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣諭曰：「製置已定，不可改易。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent word: "The arrangement is fixed and cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "The plan stands and will not change.

sentences.zh: 」如是者三。

translations.literal: " Thus three times.
translations.idiomatic: " Three times he said it.

sentences.zh: 彥等奮臂南向而罵曰：「傭保兒，敢如是也！

translations.literal: Yan and the rest waved arms southward and cursed: "Hired lackeys, how dare you!
translations.idiomatic: Yan shook his fist southward: "Bondservant brats, how dare you!

sentences.zh: 」復迫德倫列其事。

translations.literal: " They again forced Delun to list the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " They forced Delun to memorialize again.

sentences.zh: 時有文吏司空頲者，甚有筆才，彥召見，謂曰：「為我更草一狀，詞宜抵突，如更敢違，則渡河擄之。

translations.literal: At that time a clerk Sikong Ting, very skilled with the brush, was summoned by Yan, who said: "Draft another petition for me; the wording should be insulting—if they dare disobey again, we cross the river and seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Sikong Ting, a fine writer, was summoned; Yan said: "Draft a fiercer memorial—if they refuse again, we cross the Yellow River and take them.

sentences.zh: 」乃奏曰：「臣累拜封章，上聞天聽，在軍眾無非共切，何朝廷皆以為閑。

translations.literal: " He memorialized: "Your servant has repeatedly submitted sealed memorials reaching Heaven's ear; in the army none do not share the same urgency—why does the court treat all as idle?
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial ran: "We have pleaded again and again; every soldier shares this urgency—why does the court treat us as noise?

sentences.zh: 半月三軍切切，而戈予未息；

translations.literal: For half a month the three armies have been urgent while arms are not stilled;
translations.idiomatic: Half a month the host has clamored while swords stay drawn;

sentences.zh: 一城生聚皇皇，而控告無門。

translations.literal: the whole city is in turmoil yet there is no gate to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: the city trembles yet has no voice at court.

sentences.zh: 惟希俯鑒丹衷，苟從眾欲，須垂聖允，斷在不疑。

translations.literal: We only hope you will look down on our red hearts; if the multitude's wish is granted, we need your holy assent, decided without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Look on our loyal hearts; grant the army's wish without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 如或四向取謀，但慮六州俱失。

translations.literal: If you take counsel on every side, we fear all six prefectures will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitate and all six prefectures may fall.

sentences.zh: 言非意外，事在目前。

translations.literal: The words are not beyond expectation; the matter is before us now.
translations.idiomatic: This is no surprise; the crisis is now.

sentences.zh: 」張彥又以楊師厚先兼招討使，請朝廷依例授之，故復逼德倫奏曰：「臣當道兵甲素精，貔貅極銳，下視並、汾之敵，平吞鎮、定之人。

translations.literal: " Zhang Yan also asked that because Yang Shihou had once concurrently held Pacification Commissioner, the court grant it by precedent; he again forced Delun to memorialize: "Our command's arms have always been keen, our troops fiercest; we look down on Bing and Fen's foes and could swallow Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan also demanded the Pacification title Shihou once held; Delun was forced to add: "Our blades are sharp, our host the fiercest—we despise Shanxi's enemies and could take Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 特乞委臣招討之權，試臣湯火之節，苟無顯效，任賜明誅。

translations.literal: We beg to be entrusted with Pacification authority and tried in fire and water; if there is no clear effect, punish us openly.
translations.idiomatic: Give us Pacification power and test us; fail, and execute us.

sentences.zh: 」詔報曰：「魏、博寇敵接連，封疆懸遠，凡於應赴，須在師徒。

translations.literal: " The edict in reply stated: "Weibo borders enemies on every side; its frontier is far—whatever must be answered requires troops.
translations.idiomatic: " The reply read: "Weibo faces enemies on every side; distance demands armies.

sentences.zh: 是以別建節旄，各令捍禦，並、鎮則委魏、博控製，澤、潞則遣相、衛枝梧。

translations.literal: Therefore separate commands were established, each to defend; Bing and Zhen are entrusted to Weibo's control, Ze and Lu to Xiang and Wei's support.
translations.idiomatic: Separate commands were set to defend; Bing and Zhen fall to Weibo, Ze and Lu to Xiang and Wei.

sentences.zh: 咸逐便安，貴均勞逸，已定不移之制，宜從畫一之規。

translations.literal: All follow convenience for peace, balancing labor and rest—the fixed arrangement must follow one rule.
translations.idiomatic: Each post eases its sector; the division is fixed and uniform.

sentences.zh: 至於征伐事權，亦無定例。

translations.literal: As for the authority of campaigns, there is also no fixed example.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign authority has no fixed precedent either.

sentences.zh: 且臨清王領鎮之日，羅紹威守藩以來，所領事銜，本無招討。

translations.literal: When Prince of Linqing held the command and Luo Shaowei guarded the frontier, the titles held originally had no Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Linqing and Shaowei held Weibo without Pacification titles.

sentences.zh: 隻自楊師厚先除陝、滑二帥，皆以招討兼權，因茲帶過鄴中，原本不曾落下，苟循事體，寧吝施行。

translations.literal: Only when Yang Shihou was first made Shaan and Hua commander did both carry Pacification concurrently; because he passed through Ye, it was never dropped—if we follow the matter, how could we be stingy?
translations.idiomatic: Only Shihou, when made commissioner of Shaan and Hua, carried Pacification—and kept it passing through Ye; by precedent we would not withhold it.

sentences.zh: 況今劉鄩指鎮、定出征，康懷英往邠、岐進討，隻令統率師旅，亦無招討使銜。

translations.literal: Now Liu Yan marches against Zhen and Ding; Kang Huaiying advances against Bin and Qi—each leads armies without Pacification title.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan fights Zhen and Ding; Kang Huaiying Bin and Qi—neither bears Pacification.

sentences.zh: 切宜遍諭群情，勿興浮議，倚注之意，卿宜體之。

translations.literal: You must thoroughly instruct the host and not raise idle talk; our reliance on you—grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: Tell the troops plainly and end the clamor; we trust you to steady them.

sentences.zh: 」詔至，張彥壞裂，抵之於地，謂德倫曰：「梁主不達時機，聽人穿鼻，城中擾攘，未有所依。

translations.literal: " When the edict arrived Zhang Yan tore it up and threw it down, saying to Delun: "The Liang ruler does not know the times, lets men lead him by the nose; the city is in turmoil with nowhere to lean.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan shredded the edict and told Delun: "The Liang ruler is blind, led by the nose; the city has no anchor.

sentences.zh: 我甲兵雖多，須資勢援，河東晉王統兵十萬，匡復唐朝，世與大梁仇讎。

translations.literal: Our armor is many but we need backing; the Prince of Jin east of the river commands a hundred thousand, restores the Tang house, and for generations has been the Great Liang's foe.
translations.idiomatic: We have arms but need allies; the Prince of Jin holds a hundred thousand, claims to restore Tang, and has long hated Liang.

sentences.zh: 若與我同力，事無不濟，請相公改圖，以求多福。

translations.literal: If he joins us nothing will fail—please, my lord, change course and seek greater blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Join him and we prevail—change course, my lord, for fortune.

sentences.zh: 」德倫不得已而從之，乃遣牙將曹廷隱奉書求援於太原。

translations.literal: " Delun had no choice; he sent aide Cao Tingyin with a letter seeking aid from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Delun yielded and sent Cao Tingyin to Taiyuan for aid.

sentences.zh: 彥使德倫告諭軍城曰：「可依河東稱天祐十三年，此後如有人將文字於河南往來，便仰所在處置。」

translations.literal: Yan had Delun announce to the command: "Follow Hedong in calling the year Tianyou 13; hereafter if anyone carries documents to Henan, the local authorities shall deal with them."
translations.idiomatic: Yan made Delun proclaim: "Take Hedong's Tianyou year 13; any papers bound for Henan are to be seized on the road."

sentences.zh: 是月，邠州留後李保衡以城歸順。

translations.literal: That month Binzhou acting commissioner Li Baoheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Baoheng of Binzhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 保衡，楊崇本養子也。

translations.literal: Baoheng was the adopted son of Yang Chongben.
translations.idiomatic: Baoheng was adopted by Yang Chongben.

sentences.zh: 崇本乃李茂貞養子，任邠州二十餘年，去歲為其子彥魯所毒。

translations.literal: Chongben was Li Maozhen's adopted son and held Binzhou more than twenty years; last year his son Yanlu poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongben, Maozhen's adoptee, had ruled Bin twenty years until Yanlu poisoned him last year.

sentences.zh: 彥魯領知州事五十餘日，保衡殺彥魯送款於帝，即以保衡為華州節度使，以河陽留後霍彥威為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: Yanlu held the prefecture fifty-odd days; Baoheng killed Yanlu and submitted to the Emperor, who made Baoheng Huazhou Military Commissioner and Heyang acting commissioner Huo Yanwei Binzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlu ruled fifty days; Baoheng killed him and surrendered; the Emperor made Baoheng commissioner of Hua and Huo Yanwei of Bin.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，又陷澶州，刺史王彥章棄城來奔。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Cizhou was also taken; Military Commissioner Wang Yanzhang abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Cizhou fell; Wang Yanzhang fled.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Compare:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：晉人夜襲澶州，刺史王彥章在劉鄩營，晉人獲其妻子。）〉

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: Jin troops raided Cizhou by night; Military Commissioner Wang Yanzhang was in Liu Yan's camp; Jin took his wife and children.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: Jin struck Cizhou by night; Wang Yanzhang was with Liu Yan; Jin seized his family.)〉

sentences.zh: 是月，劉鄩自洹水潛師由黃澤路西趨晉陽，至樂平縣，值霖雨積旬，乃班師還。

translations.literal: That month Liu Yan secretly led troops from Huan River by the Huangze road straight toward Jinyang; reaching Leping County, they met more than ten days of rain and then turned back.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Yan stole march from Huan River toward Jinyang by Huangze; rains trapped him at Leping ten days and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次宗城，遂至貝州，軍於堂邑。

translations.literal: He halted at Zongcheng, then reached Beizhou and encamped at Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped at Zongcheng, then Beizhou, camping at Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 遇晉軍，轉鬥數十里，晉軍稍退。

translations.literal: They met Jin troops and fought for several tens of li; the Jin army gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They clashed with Jin for miles; Jin slowly gave ground.

sentences.zh: 翌日，鄩移軍於莘。

translations.literal: The next day Yan moved his army to Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Yan shifted camp to Xin.

sentences.zh: 八月，賀瑰收復澶州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month He Gui recovered Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month He Gui retook Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，以行營先鋒步軍都指揮使、行澶州刺史、檢校太保王彥章為汝州防禦使，依前行營先鋒步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month campaign vanguard foot commander, acting Cizhou prefect, Honorary Palace Attendant Wang Yanzhang was made Ruzhou Defense Commissioner, still campaign vanguard foot commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Yanzhang became defender of Ruzhou while keeping the foot vanguard.

sentences.zh: 壬午，正衙命使冊德妃張氏。

translations.literal: On renwu at the main court an envoy was ordered to invest Noble Consort Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the court sent envoys to invest Noble Consort Zhang.

sentences.zh: 是夕，妃薨。

translations.literal: That evening the consort died.
translations.idiomatic: She died that night.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛亥，康王友孜謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: On xinhai in the tenth month of winter Prince of Kang Youzi plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the tenth month Prince of Kang Youzi rebelled and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝於寢殿熟寐，忽聞禦榻上寶劍有聲，帝遽起視之，而友孜之黨已入於宮中，帝揮之獲免。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor slept soundly in the bedchamber; suddenly he heard a sound from the imperial sword on the couch; he rose at once to look, and Youzi's partisans had already entered the palace; the Emperor waved the sword and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slept deeply until his sword on the couch rang; he leapt up as Youzi's men entered the palace and drove them off with the blade.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈According to:

sentences.zh: （《清異錄》：末帝夜於寢間擒刺客，乃康王友孜所遣，帝自戮之。

translations.literal: (《Records of Unusual Matters》: At night in the bedchamber the Later Emperor seized an assassin sent by Prince of Kang Youzi and killed him himself.
translations.idiomatic: (《Records of Unusual Matters》: The Later Emperor caught an assassin sent by Youzi in the bedchamber and slew him himself.

sentences.zh: 造雲母匣貯所用劍，名匣曰「護聖將軍之館」。）〉

translations.literal: He made a mica case for the sword he used and named the case "Hall of the Guardian Sage General.")〉
translations.idiomatic: He kept the sword in a mica case called "Hall of the Guardian Sage General.")〉

sentences.zh: 壬子，葬德妃張氏。

translations.literal: On renzi Noble Consort Zhang was buried.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Noble Consort Zhang was interred.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙丑，改乾化五年為貞明元年。

translations.literal: On yichou in the eleventh month Qianhua 5 was changed to Zhenming 1.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the fifth year of Qianhua became Zhenming 1.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙未，詔升華原縣為崇州靜勝軍，以美原縣為裕州，以為屬郡。

translations.literal: On yiwei in the twelfth month an edict raised Huayuan County to Jingsheng Army of Chong Prefecture and Meiyuan County to Yu Prefecture as subject prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Huayuan became Chong Prefecture's Jingsheng Army and Meiyuan Yu Prefecture, both subordinate.

sentences.zh: 以偽命義勝軍節度使、鼎耀等州觀察使、特進、檢校太保、同平章事李彥韜為特進、檢校太傅、同平章事，充靜勝軍節度使、崇裕等州觀察使，河內郡開國侯，仍復本姓溫，名昭圖。

translations.literal: False-order Yisheng Military Commissioner, observer of Ding and Yao, Special Advancement, Honorary Palace Attendant, Co-Grand Counselor Li Yantao was made Special Advancement, Honorary Grand Mentor, Co-Grand Counselor, Jingsheng Military Commissioner and observer of Chong and Yu, Marquis of Henei Commandery, and his original surname Wen and name Zhaotu were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yantao, puppet commissioner of Yisheng, became Honorary Grand Mentor and commissioner of Jingsheng over Chong and Yu, Marquis of Henei, restored to Wen Zhaotu.

sentences.zh: 昭圖，華原賊帥也。

translations.literal: Zhaotu was a bandit chief of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaotu had been a Huayuan bandit leader.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞以為養子，以華原為耀州，美原為鼎州，偽命昭圖為節度使。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen adopted him and made Huayuan Yao Prefecture and Meiyuan Ding Prefecture, falsely appointing Zhaotu commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen adopted him, made Huayuan Yao and Meiyuan Ding, and named him commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是歸款，故有是命。

translations.literal: Now he submitted and therefore received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His surrender won him the post.

sentences.zh: 貞明二年春正月庚申，以皇伯父宋州節度使、開府儀同三司、檢校太師、兼中書令、廣王全昱為守中書令，餘如故。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the first month of spring of Zhenming 2, the Emperor's imperial uncle Songzhou Military Commissioner, Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, Prince of Guang Wang Quanyu was made acting Grand Counselor, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the first month of Zhenming 2 Prince of Guang Quanyu, the Emperor's uncle and Songzhou commissioner, became acting Grand Counselor, retaining his other titles.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈But cf.:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：二年春正月，宣武節度使、守中書令、廣德靖王全昱卒。）〉

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: In the first month of the second year, Xuanyi Military Commissioner, acting Grand Counselor, Prince of Guangde Jing Wang Quanyu died.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: That first month Xuanyi commissioner Prince of Guangde Jing Quanyu died.)〉

sentences.zh: 以浙江東道營田副使、檢校太傅、前常州刺史杜建徽遙領涇州節度使。

translations.literal: Zhejiang East Circuit farmland deputy commissioner, Honorary Grand Mentor, former Changzhou prefect Du Jianhui was given titular Jingzhou Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jianhui, Zhejiang farmland deputy and former Changzhou prefect, received titular command of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月丙申，右僕射，門下侍郎、平章事、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使楊涉罷相，守左僕射。

translations.literal: On bingshen in the second month Right Vice President of the Secretariat, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Counselor, salt and transport commissioner Yang She left the council and remained Left Vice President.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Yang She left the council, keeping only the left vice presidency.

sentences.zh: 涉累上章以疾辭位，故有是命。

translations.literal: She repeatedly memorialized illness to resign and therefore received this order.
translations.idiomatic: He had pleaded illness repeatedly and was released from the council.

sentences.zh: 是月，命許州節度使王檀、河陽節度使謝彥章、汝州防禦使王彥章率師自陰地關抵晉陽，急攻其壘，不克而還。

translations.literal: That month Xuzhou Military Commissioner Wang Tan, Heyang Military Commissioner Xie Yanzhang, and Ruzhou Defense Commissioner Wang Yanzhang led troops from Yindi Pass to Jinyang, stormed the ramparts in haste, failed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Tan, Xie Yanzhang, and Wang Yanzhang marched from Yindi Pass on Jinyang, assaulted the walls, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，劉鄩率師與晉王大戰於故元城，鄩軍敗績。

translations.literal: In the third month Liu Yan led troops in a great battle with the Prince of Jin at Old Yuancheng; Yan's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liu Yan met the Prince of Jin at Old Yuancheng and was routed.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄩駐於莘，帝以河朔危急，師老於外，餉饋不充，遣使賜鄩詔，微有責讓。

translations.literal: Earlier Yan was stationed at Xin; the Emperor, because Hebei was critical, the army long abroad, and supplies lacking, sent an edict with slight reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had camped at Xin; with Hebei desperate, the army exhausted, and grain short, the Emperor sent a reproachful edict.

sentences.zh: 鄩奏以寇勢方盛，未可輕動。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized that the enemy's momentum was still strong and one must not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied that the foe was still fierce and must not be provoked.

sentences.zh: 帝又問鄩決勝之策，鄩奏曰：「但人給糧十斛，盡則破敵。

translations.literal: The Emperor again asked Yan's plan for victory; Yan memorialized: "Only give each man ten hu of grain—when it is gone, break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked for a winning plan; Yan said: "Give every man ten hu of grain—when it runs out, we win.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，復遣促戰。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was displeased and again sent orders to hurry battle.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was angry and ordered him to fight at once.

sentences.zh: 鄩召諸將會議，諸將欲戰，鄩默然。

translations.literal: Yan summoned the generals to council; the generals wished to fight; Yan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan called his officers; they wanted battle; he said nothing.

sentences.zh: 一日，引軍攻鎮定之營，彼眾大駭，上下騰亂，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: One day he led the army to attack the Zhen-Ding camp; the enemy were greatly alarmed, upper and lower in turmoil, and very many were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: One day he struck the Zhen-Ding camp; panic swept them and many were killed or taken.

sentences.zh: 時帝遣偏將楊延直領軍萬餘人屯澶州以應鄩，既而晉王詐言歸太原，劉鄩以為信。

translations.literal: The Emperor had sent deputy general Yang Yanzhi with more than ten thousand men to camp at Cizhou in support of Yan; then the Prince of Jin falsely announced return to Taiyuan and Yan believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had posted Yang Yanzhi with ten thousand at Cizhou to support Yan; the Prince of Jin feigned retreat to Taiyuan and Yan believed him.

sentences.zh: 是月，召楊延直會於魏城下。

translations.literal: That month Yang Yanzhi was summoned to meet below Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yan called Yanzhi to Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 鄩自莘率軍亦至，與延直會。

translations.literal: Yan himself led the army from Xin and also arrived, meeting Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan marched from Xin and joined him.

sentences.zh: 既而晉王自貝州至，鄩引軍漸退，至故元城西，與晉人決戰，大為其所敗。

translations.literal: Then the Prince of Jin came from Beizhou; Yan gradually withdrew; reaching west of Old Yuancheng he fought the Jin to the decision and was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin came from Beizhou; Yan fell back to Old Yuancheng and was shattered in the decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 追襲至河上，軍士赴水死者甚眾，鄩自黎陽濟河奔滑州。

translations.literal: Pursuit reached the river; very many soldiers drowned going into the water; Yan crossed at Liyang and fled to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuit drove men into the river by the thousands; Yan crossed at Liyang and fled to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，製以鄩為滑州宣義軍節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: On jisi an ordinance made Yan Xuanyi Military Commissioner deputy and knowing commissioner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Yan was made Xuanyi deputy and acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉人攻衛州，陷之；

translations.literal: Jin troops attacked Weizhou and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Jin took Weizhou;

sentences.zh: 又攻惠州。

translations.literal: they also attacked Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: then besieged Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙酉朔，威武軍節度使、守太傅、兼中書令、閩王王審知賜號忠勤保安興國功臣，餘如故。

translations.literal: On yiyou, first day of the fourth month of summer, Weiwu Military Commissioner, acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, Prince of Min Wang Shenzhi was granted the title of Loyal, Diligent, Security, and Revival Merit Lord, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, first of the fourth month, Prince of Min Wang Shenzhi received the merit title Loyal, Diligent, Security, and Revival Lord, retaining his other ranks.

sentences.zh: 晉人陷洺州。

translations.literal: Jin troops took Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin seized Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯夜，捉生都將李霸作亂，龍驤都將杜晏球討平之。

translations.literal: On the night of guimao the captive-recruiting commander Li Ba rebelled; Dragon-Prancing commander Du Yanqiu suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao night Li Ba of the captive-recruiters mutinied; Du Yanqiu of Dragon-Prancing crushed him.

sentences.zh: 時遣捉生軍千人戌楊劉，軍出宋門外。

translations.literal: A thousand captive-recruit troops had been sent to garrison Yangliu; the army went out beyond Song Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand captive-recruits garrisoned Yangliu and had marched out through Song Gate.

sentences.zh: 是夜，由水門復入，二鼓大噪，火發燭城，李霸與其徒燔建國門，不克。

translations.literal: That night they re-entered by the water gate; at the second watch they raised a great clamor and fire lit the city; Li Ba and his followers burned the Jianguo Gate but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: That night they came back through the water gate; at the second watch fire and uproar filled the capital; Ba burned Jianguo Gate but failed to break it.

sentences.zh: 龍驤都將杜晏球屯鞠場，聞亂兵至，率騎擊之，亂軍退，走馬登建國門。

translations.literal: Dragon-Prancing commander Du Yanqiu was encamped at the ball court; hearing the rebels come, he led cavalry to strike; the rebels retreated and ran to mount the Jianguo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanqiu at the ball court heard the alarm, charged with horse, and drove the rebels toward Jianguo Gate.

sentences.zh: 晏球奏曰：「亂者惟李霸一軍，但守宮城，遲明，臣必破之。

translations.literal: Yanqiu memorialized: "The rebels are only Li Ba's one army—just hold the palace; at dawn I will break them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu reported: "Only Li Ba's band rebels—hold the palace; by dawn I will destroy them.

sentences.zh: 」未明，晏球誅霸及其同惡，京師方定。

translations.literal: " Before light Yanqiu killed Ba and his accomplices and the capital was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Before dawn he killed Ba and his fellows and the capital was calm.

sentences.zh: 是月，以行營先鋒步軍都指揮使、汝州防禦使王彥章為鄭州防禦使，依前先鋒步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: That month campaign vanguard foot commander and Ruzhou Defense Commissioner Wang Yanzhang was made Zhengzhou Defense Commissioner, still vanguard foot commander.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Yanzhang became defender of Zhengzhou while keeping the foot vanguard.

sentences.zh: 五月，晉軍還太原。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Jin army returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jin withdrew to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，晉人急攻邢州，帝遣捉生都將張溫率步騎五百人入於邢州，至內黃，溫率眾降於晉人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Jin urgently attacked Xingzhou; the Emperor sent captive-recruiting commander Zhang Wen with five hundred foot and horse into Xingzhou; reaching Neihuang, Wen led his men in surrender to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jin besieged Xingzhou; the Emperor sent Zhang Wen with five hundred troops; at Neihuang Wen defected to Jin.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲寅朔，晉王自太原至魏州，節度使張筠棄城奔京師，邢州節度使閻寶以城降於晉王。

translations.literal: On jiayin, first day of the seventh month of autumn, the Prince of Jin came from Taiyuan to Weizhou; Military Commissioner Zhang Jun abandoned the city and fled to the capital; Xingzhou Military Commissioner Yan Bao surrendered the city to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, first of the seventh month, the Prince of Jin reached Weizhou; Zhang Jun fled to court; Yan Bao of Xingzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以淮南鎮海鎮東等軍節度使、充淮南宣潤等道西面行營都統、開府儀同三司、尚父、守尚書令、吳越王錢鏐為諸道兵馬元帥，餘如故。

translations.literal: On renxu Huainan, Zhenhai, and Zhendong Military Commissioner, commander of the Huainan-Xuan-Run western campaign, Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, Imperial Father, acting Secretariat Director, Prince of Wu Qian Liu was made Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits' Armies and Horses, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Qian Liu of Wu, commander of Huainan and the western campaign, became Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits, retaining his other honors.

sentences.zh: 以左僕射楊涉為太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: Left Vice President Yang She was made Heir Apparent Grand Tutor and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She retired as Heir Apparent Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 八月丁酉，以開府儀同三司、太子太保致仕趙光逢為司空兼門下侍郎、平章事、宏文館大學士、延資庫使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: On dingyou Grand Preceptor of the Palace Gate, Heir Apparent Grand Mentor retired Zhao Guangfeng was made Minister of Works, Concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Counselor, Hongwen University Chancellor, and Extending Treasury Commissioner, and made salt and transport commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Zhao Guangfeng, retired Heir Apparent Grand Mentor, returned as minister of works, co-counselor, Hongwen chancellor, treasury commissioner, and salt and transport chief.

sentences.zh: 九月，晉王還太原。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Prince of Jin returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Prince of Jin went back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 滄州節度使戴思遠棄城來奔，晉人陷貝州。

translations.literal: Cangzhou Military Commissioner Dai Siyuan abandoned the city and fled; Jin took Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Siyuan fled Cangzhou; Jin took Beizhou.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈From:

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》本紀：二年九月，晉人克貝州，守將張源德死之。

translations.literal: (《New History of the Tang: Basic Annals》: In the ninth month of the second year Jin took Beizhou; defending general Zhang Yuande died.
translations.idiomatic: (《New History of the Tang: Basic Annals》: In the ninth month of year two Jin took Beizhou; defender Zhang Yuande died.

sentences.zh: 又，《死事傳》略云：太祖時，源德自金吾衛將軍為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: Also, 《Biographies of Those Who Died for the State》 in brief: In Taizu's time Yuande went from Golden Crow Guard general to Caizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: 《Biographies of Those Who Died for the State》 adds: Under Taizu, Yuande went from Golden Crow guard to Caizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 貞明元年，魏博節度使楊師厚卒，末帝分魏、相等六州為兩鎮，遣劉鄩將兵萬人屯於魏。

translations.literal: In Zhenming 1, Weibo Military Commissioner Yang Shihou died; the Later Emperor divided Wei, Xiang, and the other six prefectures into two commands and sent Liu Yan with ten thousand troops to camp at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 1, when Shihou died, the Later Emperor split Weibo and sent Liu Yan with ten thousand to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏軍叛降晉，源德為鄩守貝州。

translations.literal: The Weibo army rebelled and surrendered to Jin; Yuande defended Beizhou for Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo mutinied to Jin; Yuande held Beizhou for Yan.

sentences.zh: 晉王入魏，諸將欲先擊貝州，晉王曰：「貝城小而堅，攻之難卒下。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin entered Wei the generals wished to strike Beizhou first; the Prince of Jin said: "Bei city is small and firm—hard to take quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin entered Wei his officers wanted Beizhou first; he said: "Bei is small and hard—do not linger.

sentences.zh: 」乃先襲破德州，然後以兵五千攻源德，源德堅守不下，晉軍塹而圍之。

translations.literal: " He first raided and broke Dezhou, then attacked Yuande with five thousand troops; Yuande held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: " He smashed Dezhou first, then besieged Yuande with five thousand; Yuande held.

sentences.zh: 已而劉鄩大敗於故元城，南走黎陽，六鎮數十州之地皆歸晉，獨貝一州，圍之逾年不可下。

translations.literal: Soon Liu Yan was greatly defeated at Old Yuancheng and fled south to Liyang; dozens of commands and prefectures of the six commands returned to Jin—only Bei one prefecture was besieged more than a year without fall.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan was routed at Old Yuancheng and fled, Hebei fell to Jin—all but Bei, besieged more than a year.

sentences.zh: 源德守既堅，而貝人聞晉已盡有河北，城中食且盡，乃勸源德出降，源德不從，遂見殺。）〉

translations.literal: Yuande's defense was firm and the people of Bei heard Jin already held Hebei; food in the city was nearly gone; they urged Yuande to surrender but he would not and was therefore killed.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuande held on until Bei's grain was gone and the people knew Jin owned Hebei; they begged him to yield; he refused and was slain.)〉

sentences.zh: 己卯，天平軍節度副大使、知節度事、檢校太師、兼中書令、琅琊郡王王檀薨。

translations.literal: On jimao Tianping Military Commissioner deputy, knowing commissioner affairs, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, Prince of Langya Wang Tan died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Wang Tan of Tianping, Prince of Langya, died.
